message.content:
**Your 7‑Day Paris Adventure – A Complete Trip Plan**

> *“Paris is not a place, it’s a feeling.”* – Anonymous  
> *Let’s turn that feeling into a 7‑day itinerary that balances culture, cuisine, and a touch of luxury.*

---

## 1️⃣ Pre‑Trip Checklist

| Item | Details | Tips |
|------|---------|------|
| **Passport & Visa** | Valid for at least 6 months. EU/US/Canada/UK passports usually don’t need a visa for stays <90 days. | Check the French consulate website for your country. |
| **Travel Insurance** | Medical, trip cancellation, baggage. | Look for “European coverage” and “COVID‑19 protection.” |
| **Flights** | Book 2–3 months ahead for best fares. | Use fare alerts (Google Flights, Skyscanner). |
| **Accommodation** | 4‑star boutique hotel or Airbnb in Le Marais or Saint‑Germain. | Book with free cancellation. |
| **Currency** | Euro (€). | Get a small amount of cash on arrival; use a travel card for larger purchases. |
| **Packing** | Light layers, comfortable shoes, umbrella, power adapter (Type C/F). | Pack a small day‑pack for museum visits. |
| **Apps** | Citymapper, Google Maps, RATP (public transport), Duolingo (basic French). | Download offline maps. |

---

## 2️⃣ Day‑by‑Day Itinerary

| Day | Morning | Lunch | Afternoon | Evening |
|-----|---------|-------|-----------|---------|
| **Day 1 – Arrival & Settling In** | Arrive at Charles de Gaulle. Take the RER B to Gare du Nord → Metro Line 4 to **Le Marais**. | Café **Café Charlot** (classic French bistro). | Walk along **Rue des Rosiers** (Jewish quarter), visit **Picasso Museum**. | Dinner at **Le Comptoir du Relais** (bistro‑style). |
| **Day 2 – Classic Landmarks** | Early visit to **Eiffel Tower** (skip‑the‑line ticket). | Picnic at **Champ de Mars** (grab baguette, cheese, wine). | Stroll along the Seine, cross to **Louvre** (pre‑book tickets). | Sunset cruise on the Seine (Bateaux Mouches). |
| **Day 3 – Artistic Vibes** | Explore **Montmartre**: Sacré‑Coeur, Place du Tertre. | Lunch at **Le Consulat** (historic café). | Visit **Musée d’Orsay** (Impressionist masterpieces). | Dinner at **Le Cinq** (Michelin‑star) or a cozy **crêperie**. |
| **Day 4 – Hidden Gems** | Start at **Parc des Buttes‑Chaumont** (great views). | Brunch at **Holybelly 5** (Australian‑French fusion). | Wander through **Canal Saint‑Martin**, pop into quirky shops. | Night walk along **Pont Alexandre III** (illuminated). |
| **Day 5 – Day Trip** | Take a train to **Versailles** (RER C). | Picnic in the gardens or lunch at **La Petite Venise**. | Tour the Hall of Mirrors, the Grand Trianon. | Return to Paris, dinner at **L’Atelier de Joël Robuchon**. |
| **Day 6 – Modern & Shopping** | Visit **Centre Pompidou** (modern art). | Lunch at **Le Georges** (roof‑top restaurant). | Shopping on **Boulevard Haussmann** (Galeries Lafayette, Printemps). | Attend a show at **Opéra Garnier** (if available). |
| **Day 7 – Relax & Departure** | Brunch at **Café de Flore** (iconic spot). | Last‑minute souvenir shopping at **Marché aux Puces de Saint‑Ouen**. | Pack, check‑out, head to the airport. | Optional: late‑night flight or stay an extra night. |

---

## 3️⃣ Budget Breakdown (per person)

| Category | Approx. Cost (€) |
|----------|------------------|
| Flights (round‑trip) | 350–600 |
| Accommodation (6 nights) | 900–1,200 |
| Food & Drinks | 400–600 |
| Attractions & Tours | 250–350 |
| Transport (metro, RER, day trips) | 100–150 |
| Miscellaneous (souvenirs, tips) | 100–150 |
| **Total** | **2,100 – 3,000** |

> *Adjust based on your preferences (luxury vs. budget).*

---

## 4️⃣ Transportation Tips

| Mode | How to Use | Cost |
|------|------------|------|
| **Metro & RER** | Buy a **carnet** of 10 tickets (€14.90) or a **Paris Visite pass** (daily/3‑day). | €1.90 per ride (carnet) |
| **Bus** | Same as metro. | €1.90 |
| **Taxi/Uber** | Use the app; meter starts at €2.60 + €0.25/km. | €20–30 for airport transfer |
| **Bike (Vélib’)** | Rent a bike for a day (€12.50). | €12.50 |
| **Walking** | Many attractions are within walking distance. | Free |

---

## 5️⃣ Dining Highlights

| Cuisine | Restaurant | Why |
|---------|------------|-----|
| Classic French | **Le Comptoir du Relais** | Intimate bistro, seasonal menu |
| Seafood | **Septime** | Contemporary, sustainable |
| Street Food | **L’As du Fallafel** (Le Marais) | Legendary falafel |
| Vegan | **Le Potager du Marais** | Plant‑based French |
| Dessert | **Pierre Hermé** | World‑famous macarons |

---

## 6️⃣ Language & Etiquette

| Phrase | Translation | When to Use |
|--------|-------------|-------------|
| Bonjour / Bonsoir | Hello / Good evening | Greeting |
| Merci beaucoup | Thank you very much | After service |
| Parlez‑vous anglais? | Do you speak English? | If needed |
| Où est…? | Where is…? | Directions |
| Je voudrais… | I would like… | Ordering food |

> *A few polite words go a long way.*

---

## 7️⃣ Safety & Health

- Keep an eye on your belongings in crowded areas.
- Carry a reusable water bottle (water is safe to drink).
- If you have allergies, bring a copy of your medication in English.
- Stay hydrated, especially if you’re exploring outdoors.

---

## 8️⃣ Quick Reference Map

- **Le Marais** – Central, historic district.
- **Eiffel Tower** – Near Champ de Mars.
- **Louvre** – Right next to Palais Royal.
- **Montmartre** – North‑west hill.
- **Versailles** – West of Paris, 30‑min RER C ride.

*(Attach a simple map image or link to Google Maps for visual reference.)*

---

### Final Thought

Paris is a city that invites you to pause, taste, and marvel. With this plan, you’ll experience its iconic sights, hidden corners, and culinary delights—all while staying organized and budget‑friendly. Bon voyage! 🌍✈️🍷
